question.text:
What will happen when the following code is compiled?

#include <stdio.h>

int x = 5;

int main() {
    extern int x;
    int x = 10;

    printf("%d", x);

    return 0;
}
  1. $\texttt{5}$
     
  2. $\texttt{10}$
     
  3. Compilation error
     
  4. Linker error
question.subject: Programming in C

question.text:
What is the output of the following code?

#include <stdio.h>

int a = 1;

void fun() {
    static int a = 2;
    a++;
    printf("%d ", a);
}

int main() {
    auto int b = 5;

    fun();

    {
        extern int a;
        printf("%d ", a);
    }

    fun();

    printf("%d", b);

    return 0;
}
  1. $\texttt{3\ 1\ 4\ 5}$
     
  2. $\texttt{3\ 2\ 4\ 5}$
     
  3. $\texttt{2\ 1\ 3\ 5}$
     
  4. Compilation error
question.subject: Programming in C

Which of the following statements is correct in C?

  1. An automatic local variable has block scope and lifetime throughout the program execution
     
  2. A static local variable has block scope and lifetime throughout the program execution
     
  3. A static global variable has external linkage
     
  4. A register variable must always be stored in a CPU register

question.text:
What is the output of the following code?

#include <stdio.h>

void f() {
    static int x = 0;
    x = x + 2;
    printf("%d ", x);
}

void g() {
    static int x = 5;
    x = x + 3;
    printf("%d ", x);
}

int main() {
    f();
    g();
    f();
    g();

    return 0;
}
  1. $\texttt{2\ 8\ 4\ 11}$
     
  2. $\texttt{2\ 5\ 4\ 8}$
     
  3. $\texttt{2\ 8\ 2\ 8}$
     
  4. $\texttt{0\ 5\ 2\ 8}$
